trickyParts: The tester named one site; the same shape is at nine. Each is a state change, one rig.tick(), then an immediate len(rig.replacements()) != 1 with no wait, and each asks the same question of the same deferral. The architect approved wiring all of them in this commit rather than the one CI happened to catch (Envoy, 2026-11-01T20:26:49Z), after I reported the list.

Every assertion that a replacement has NOT happened is left reading the count once, as the architect directed: a deferral cannot turn nothing-yet into a spurious replacement, so those are sound as they stand. The subtest table at podupdate_test.go's end-under-test case is left alone too: it already awaits the round ending before it reads the count.

awaitReplacement sweeps rather than merely polling, because in this rig a sweep happens only when the test calls tick(): the production rule is that the next sweep makes the replacement, so waiting without sweeping would wait for ever. It checks the count before its first tick, so a test whose replacement already happened at its own tick does no extra sweep, and it stops at the first poll that reaches n, so it never overshoots. The rig's clock is held, so the extra sweeps re-task nobody and trip no notice bound.

The round's forward merge is main's accountDrift meeting this branch's update round. The resolved `replace` keeps accountDrifted unconditional and leaves the image term deleted: a ServiceAccount is fixed for a pod's life, PodDrift does not read it, and no stale-plugin install can move it, so a launch is the only thing that replaces such a pod, where an issue pod's image drift is the round's. internal/runtime/sandbox passing whole is what proves the union, since both sides' tests are in it.
deviations: The architect asked for the daemon package to run inside the full suite with 0 failures. It cannot in this pod: internal/daemon's test binary aborts on the first test that starts a NATS testcontainer, and this pod has no docker. Fifteen such tests were enumerated by skipping them one at a time before I stopped; they are spread across daemon_test.go, blockers_scratch_dispatch_test.go, notice_exceptions_test.go, outbox_scratch_dispatch_test.go and person_handover_scratch_dispatch_test.go and the helpers they share. What is run instead, and quoted above: the nine touched tests at -count=100 (900 runs, 0 failures), the whole pod-update family at -count=1 (35 PASS), and the full ./internal/... ./cmd/... suite with its failure set accounted for test by test.
CI at the code head had not concluded when this phase completed: run 41356135250 was still pending at 22:15Z, seconds after the push. The reviewer reads the head's checks itself before it approves.

discoveredComplexity: The `permission denied to terminate process (SQLSTATE 42501)` that the previous round's handoff put down to a sibling role sharing the pod's PostgreSQL is not that. It reproduces on a server with no other role on it at all: isolatedOutboxPool's teardown runs `drop database … with (force)`, which terminates the backends still connected to that database, and legion_test is not a superuser and holds no pg_signal_backend, so Postgres refuses. Granting pg_signal_backend to legion_test on this role's own throwaway server made 900 runs green where the same selection had failed in teardown on both the pod's shared server and the ungranted private one. It is a teardown failure and never an assertion, and CI's own PostgreSQL does not show it. The previous round's discoveredComplexity entry is corrected by this one.

Three suites still cannot run in this pod, for the environment and not for the change: internal/runtime/tmux's TestNewRefusesLaunchersItCannotRun (tmux is not installed), every test that starts a NATS testcontainer (no docker), and pi-legion's judge-omp rig (each judge runs in a container).
